paper_sections.title: Arithmetic in two languages: Localizing simple multiplication processing in the adult bilingual brain

description.value: The study investigated whether simple multiplication processing differs between bilingual adults’ language of learning and their other language, using behavioral measures and fMRI, with problem size and language proficiency also examined.

design.value: Thirty-five Spanish-English bilingual adults completed two localizer tasks and an experimental single-digit multiplication verification task in one fMRI session; six participants were excluded and analyses included 29 participants. The multiplication and verbal localizer tasks were administered in English and Spanish, with language order alternated across participants.

description.value: Test 14: Picture Vocabulary and Test 15: Oral Comprehension were used to determine English language proficiency.
Equivalent Spanish versions of the language proficiency tests were administered, including Vocabulario Sobre Dibujos and Oral Comprehension.
Test 8: Incomplete words was used to assess phonological awareness in each language.

name.value: Math Fluency: Multiplication subtest of the Wechsler Individual Achievement Test (WIAT)

description.value: Participants answered as many single-digit multiplication problems as possible in 60 seconds.
Handedness was assessed using the Edinburgh Inventory; scores ranged from 0.35 to 1.00.
A measure of working memory was collected for use outside the scope of the current research questions.

description.value: Thirty-five Spanish-English bilingual adults were recruited for this study, with 5 from the University of Texas at Austin and 30 from the University of Houston. The final sample comprised 29 participants.

excluded_count.value: Six of the initial 35 participants were excluded from the final sample.

inclusion_criteria.value: only bilinguals who learned both languages before 9 years old with equivalent proficiency across languages were included in the analyses

Participants were right-handed, had normal or corrected-to-normal vision, normal hearing, no history of cognitive or perceptual deficits, were not diagnosed with language delays or learning disabilities, and were not taking medication that affected their cognition at the time of testing.

diagnostic_instrument.value: Woodcock-Johnson Tests of Achievement, Woodcock-Johnson Tests of Cognitive Abilities, and Batería III Woodcock-Munoz

clinical_characteristics.value: All participants reported Spanish as their native language (L1), with 8 participants also reporting English as a simultaneous native language. Eleven individuals learned multiplication in Spanish, and 18 reported learning multiplication in English. All participants reported using English as their current preferred math language, with 2 additionally reporting a preference for Spanish depending on context.

medication_status.value: one participant was excluded due to taking psychoactive medications at the time of testing; participants were not taking medication that affected their cognition at the time of testing

task_description.value: Participants heard two spoken number words, followed by a visual Arabic digit, and determined whether the Arabic digit was the correct product of the two spoken numbers. They completed two runs in English and two runs in Spanish.

instructions.value: Participants were instructed to determine whether the proposed solution was true or false and responded with their right hand; they used their index finger if the proposed solution was true and their middle finger if it was false.

stimuli.value: Two spoken number words followed by a visual Arabic digit; proposed solutions were presented as Arabic digits and participants did not see written words.

task_description.value: Participants saw a black-and-white line drawing of an object followed by a spoken word and determined whether the word matched the presented picture. They completed two runs in English and two runs in Spanish.

instructions.value: Participants determined whether the spoken word matched the presented picture or not.

stimuli.value: Black-and-white line drawing of an object followed by a spoken word.

task_description.value: Participants determined which of two sequentially presented dot arrays contained more dots. They completed two runs.

instructions.value: Participants were tasked with determining which of two sequentially presented dot arrays contained more dots.

stimuli.value: Sequentially presented dot arrays; comparisons had ratios of 1:3, 1:2, or 2:3.

modality.value: fMRI blood oxygenation level dependent (BOLD) signal

instrument.value: Siemens Prisma Fit scanner (3T) at the Baylor College of Medicine’s Core for Advanced Magnetic Resonance Imaging and Siemens Skyra scanner (3T) at the University of Texas’s Biomedical Imaging Center

description.value: The fMRI BOLD signal was measured with a susceptibility-weighted single-shot echo planar imaging (EPI) sequence. Parameters across both scanners were TE = 30 ms, flip angle = 68 s, matrix size = 256 x 256, field of view = 256, slice thickness = 2 mm, number of slices = 64, TR = 1,250 ms, and voxel size 2 x 2 x 2 mm.

instrument.value: Siemens Prisma Fit scanner (3T) and Siemens Skyra scanner (3T)

description.value: Before functional image acquisition, a high-resolution T1-weighted 3D structural image was acquired for each participant with TR = 1,900 ms, TE = 2.43 ms, matrix size = 256 x 256, field of view = 256 mm, slice thickness = 1 mm, and number of slices = 192.

Functional images were realigned to their mean functional image across runs; anatomical segmentation products were combined to create a brain mask and skull-stripped anatomical image; functional images were co-registered, normalized to the standard T1 MNI template, smoothed, and motion outliers were identified and repaired by interpolation.

steps.value: realignment to the mean functional image across runs
anatomical segmentation and creation of an anatomical brain mask
skull stripping of the anatomical image
co-registration of the mean and all functional images to the skull-stripped anatomical image
normalization to the standard T1 Montreal Neurological Institute (MNI) template
smoothing with a 6 mm isotropic Gaussian kernel
identification and interpolation repair of outlier volumes
deweighting repaired volumes in first-level modeling

model_settings.value: Activation was modeled as epochs time-locked to the first stimulus in each trial. All proposed solutions and all participants’ responses were included in the model. Time series data were high-pass filtered at 1/128 Hz, and serial correlations were corrected using an autoregressive AR model. Six motion parameters estimated during realignment were entered in the first-level modeling as regressors, and repaired volumes were deweighted.
Subjects were included as a random effect. Satterthwaite’s method was used to estimate denominator degrees of freedom for F statistics.

estimator.value: generalized linear model from the lme4 package in R

model_settings.value: Models included Problem Size, Language, and the additive effect with and without the interaction between the two. The Watanabe information criteria comparison (WAIC) determined model fit, and posterior summaries provided Bayesian p-values.
